title: feat(objectql,core): one tenant read predicate for Layer 0 and every driver (ADR-0131 C8 stage 8a)
body:
Part of #15212
Clause-②: yes

ADR-0131 C8, **stage 8a — one tenant read predicate (D8)**, per the stage plan 6251466182 and the claim 6251491183. #15831 (the driver leg ignored `platformGlobalObjects`) is closed by pointer after this merges; its tripwire pin already reads 2 (measured below).

## What changed

- **One function decides.** `computeTenantLayer0Verdict` and `TenantLayer0Input` move to `packages/core/src/security/tenant-layer0-verdict.ts` (new `@objectstack/core` export). `plugin-security`'s `tenant-layer.ts` re-exports and calls it; its Layer 0 filter, the recorded verdict and the intersect are byte-identical.
- **The engine projects that verdict onto the driver.** `buildDriverOptions` (`packages/objectql/src/engine.ts`) no longer derives `DriverOptions.tenantId` / `tenantIds` on its own. For a read, count, aggregate, update or delete it projects:
  - the verdict the wall RECORDED on this operation (`OperationContext.tenantLayer0Verdict`, parsed with `TenantLayer0VerdictSchema`), where the security layer composed its wall. That verdict carries the exempt `PLATFORM_ADMIN`, the verified owner's read lift and the delegator intersection;
  - otherwise the same function over the engine's own facts: the posture in force (`resolveEnginePosture`), the context's organization and membership set, no admin exemption. This covers a system context, a by-id write, and a composition with no security layer.
  - Projection: `none` → no scope; `organization` → `tenantId`; `organizations` → `tenantIds` (with the active organization as `tenantId`, which the driver keys on); `deny` → the active organization if any (the narrowest scope a driver can express).
- **The write target is untouched.** The insert path passes `writeTarget: true` and keeps the active organization as `tenantId` (and the `group` membership set) in every posture, so the row stamp and the counter scope hold. The engine has no upsert door (`ENGINE_UPDATE_UPSERT_REMOVED`); the SQL driver's own upsert cross-organization conflict refusal is reached only by direct driver callers and is untouched by this change. (Wording corrected by the epic seat from contract review 6254710664 ①(d).)
- **Not touched:** both `orWhereNull` arms in `sql-driver.ts` (stage 8c-1), `sharing-rule-service.ts`, the ownership ceremony, and the 8b-0a / 8b-0b producers.
- Docblocks that described the double derivation are corrected (`buildDriverOptions`, `memory-tenancy-guard.ts`). ADR-0087 semantic entry `driver-read-scope-follows-tenant-wall`; changeset `15212-8a-one-predicate.md`.

## Clause-② — what widens

| posture / caller | driver scope before | driver scope now |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `single`, a caller naming an organization | that organization (plus organization-less rows) | none |
| walled, exempt `PLATFORM_ADMIN` on a posture-permitting object, or the verified owner's read | the active organization | none (what Layer 0 already admits) |
| `isolated` / `group` member; walled system context naming an organization | equality / union | unchanged |

**Consequence, settled by ADR-0131 D8/D11:** a `single` install holding more than one organization (the `org_bu` dogfood fixture shape) loses the driver isolation it had by accident. `single` enforces no wall. Organizations are kept apart on `isolated` / `group`.

## Mechanism assumptions (Section 2), measured

- **A1 — holds.** `buildDriverOptions` derived `tenantId` from `execCtx.tenantId` alone (and `tenantIds` only via the provider's `group`). Implemented as above.
- **A2 — holds.** `@objectstack/objectql` and `@objectstack/plugin-security` both already depend on `@objectstack/core`, and `core` depends on neither. `check-undeclared-dep-imports` is green.
- **A3 — already true before this PR.** `tenant-layer0-verdict-end-to-end.test.ts:181` reads `toBe(2)` on `main`. ADR-0131 D7 (C6) made the carve-out total: a declared object is planned with no organization column, so the driver has nothing to scope. This PR leaves that pin as it is.
- **A4 — holds,** with the table above.
- **A5 — measured.** 8-M's heuristic counted up to 38 suites. The suites that actually failed were 13 files across 6 packages:
  - objectql: `engine.test.ts`, `engine-external-tenant-scope`, `engine-reference-tenant-scope`, `engine-findone-contract`, `engine-aggregate-search`;
  - plugin-security: `explain-enforce-parity`;
  - plugin-sharing: `rule-criteria-org-scope`, `record-share-organization-stamp`;
  - service-storage: `chunk-part-record-concurrency`;
  - dogfood: `schedule-sweep-organization-scope`, `schedule-acting-organization`, `invitation-ledger-row-scope`.
  
  Each pin that asserted cross-organization isolation now runs under an explicit `isolated` posture. The `single` cases assert the widened answer. In `explain-enforce-parity`, the `NATIVE_SCOPING_UNDER_SINGLE` "measured divergence" joins the invariant: explain and enforcement now agree under `single`.
- **A6 — holds.** 1,008 changed lines in total (763 added, 245 deleted, 20 files): 609 in source, changeset and entry, and 399 in tests.

**Landing points outside the claim's named list.** These are the default-posture suites the claim's last bullet covers, measured above: `service-storage/src/chunk-part-record-concurrency.test.ts`, `plugin-sharing/src/record-share-organization-stamp.test.ts`, and the three dogfood suites. No source file outside the claim surface was edited.

## Verification (on `cc6801a0e`, `main` merged)

- **Package suites:**
  - objectql: 444 files, 8,337 passed.
  - plugin-security: 187 files, 3,736 passed, 45 skipped.
  - plugin-sharing: 1,117 passed. service-storage: 1,041 passed. core: 2,634 passed.
- **Dogfood:** all 8 shards, 2,266 passed, 18 skipped, 0 failed.
- **Before the merge** (same diff): driver-sql 3,677 passed; runtime (4 shards) 7,414 passed; plugin-audit, plugin-auth, plugin-approvals, plugin-email, organizations, driver-memory, service-messaging, service-settings, service-analytics, service-mailbox and service-automation all green.
  - `@objectstack/rest`: only the ObjectQL-with-tenant suite was run (52 passed), because the full suite is longer than the foreground cap. CI runs the rest.
- **Typecheck green:** core, objectql, plugin-security, plugin-sharing, service-storage, driver-memory, dogfood, spec.
- **Ablation** (`scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, test reads `src/`): re-adding the active-organization scope on a `none` verdict reddens exactly the two widening pins in `engine-driver-read-scope.test.ts` (2 failed, 11 passed). The restore was verified: blob equals HEAD and `git diff HEAD` is empty.
- **Gates:** `dispatch-gates --commands` derived 100 families, and `--ran` reconciled 100 run with 0 NOT-MEASURED. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated` is green, and `check:adr-0087-registration` reads 1 non-breaking changeset.

## Acceptance notes

- **On a `single` install, an org-bound session's reads no longer reach the memory driver with a tenant scope.** The guard's seam 3 judges whatever scope arrives. Writes still carry the target, so the memory driver still refuses them.
- **The `@objectstack/verify` harness comment is now stale.** It says the audience-gate invitations under `org_verify_audience_gate` are invisible to fixtures (`harness.ts`, `inviteForAudienceGate`). On `single` they are now visible to the owner, and `invitation-ledger-row-scope` filters them. The comment was left as it is because it is outside this stage's surface.
- **The schedule dogfood suites set the engine's posture provider to `isolated` around the bind.** They model a walled deployment without booting the enterprise organizations plugin, and the driver scope now follows the engine's posture rather than the context's organization alone.
